registered: 2026-10-29, after the development runs listed under known_before_registration and before the registered run of run.sh
critique: 9 (leaky projections): code printed by `rce emit` is not idiomatic and does not work with the libraries of its language's ecosystem (PyTorch or FastAPI in Python, Tokio in Rust, React in TypeScript or JavaScript).
question: At one public commit of openIE-dev/rce, (a) can a program printed by `rce emit python|rust|js` be driven as a step function by an ordinary host built on its ecosystem's libraries, with a transcript equal to `rce run` byte for byte; (b) how many lines is the emitted code against a hand-written idiomatic version of the same program; (c) how much hand-written glue does each host need; and (d) what does one call cost at the boundary (JSON to the event value, the step, the state to JSON), in nanoseconds?

run_commit.base: 8ce91cea (main), whose rce is the `before` binary of M4
run_commit.changes: examples/interop/ (hosts, adapters, hand-written versions, check.py, streams.json); the emitter: the Python observations run under __name__ == "__main__", the JavaScript observations run only when node runs the file and the module exports its step API and loads without `process`, the Rust initial_state, show_state and event_fields are pub; .github/workflows/interop.yml. The statement of the embedding in spec 10.5 and the regenerated spec files follow in a later commit that changes no code

population: eight programs of spec/examples that declare state, events and steps: 01_counter, 04_bank_account, 16_multi_region, 17_traffic_light, 30_state_machine_guarded, 31_inventory, 55_rcedb, 58_float_keys (integers of four widths, text, f64 with -0.0 and 0.0 as separate map keys, lists, maps, two regions, a kind, emitted outputs and kept steps). Eleven event streams, fixed in examples/interop/streams.json, written before registration; a stream's kept step, when it has one, is its last event.

measures.M1_loc: for each program and language (python, js, rust): counted lines of the emitted file, split at the end of the runtime (the LOOP_LIMIT line, and for JS `const KC = {};`) and at the start of the driver (`def observe()`, `function observe()`, `fn main()`): runtime, program (between the two) and driver; and counted lines of the program's section of hand/LANG/programs.* (from its `---- NAME` marker to the next). Counted line: not blank and not only a comment (# or //); Python docstring lines are comments. Primary figure: program lines over hand lines, per program and summed over the eight.
measures.M2_glue: counted lines of each host's glue files (python/rce_host.py, service.py, fastapi_app.py, numpy_drive.py; js/rce_host.mjs, service.mjs, Program.mjs, react_drive.mjs, browser_drive.mjs; rust/src/adapter.rs, main.rs, bench.rs), of the hand versions' drivers, and the number of glue lines that name one of the eight programs (per-program glue).
measures.M3_boundary_cost: per call over stream 0 of each program: decode (JSON text to the event value the step takes: json.loads + adapter in Python, JSON.parse with source text + adapter in JS, serde_json + adapter in Rust), step (fuel reset + delta), encode (the state to canonical JSON text: fv_json(form_value) in Python and JS, serde_json from the adapter's value_json in Rust). Timers: time.perf_counter_ns, process.hrtime.bigint, std::time::Instant, read around each phase (the timer's own cost is inside each phase). Passes over the stream: Python 300, JS 3000, Rust 20000; 5 repetitions; reported: the median over repetitions of the mean per call, rounded to 1 ns. The hand versions are timed the same way (decode = JSON to the event dict, object or serde enum; step; encode = JSON of the state in Python and JS, the display text in Rust). Boundary share = (decode + encode) / (decode + step + encode).
measures.M4_embedding: examples/interop/check.py with every runner (python, fastapi, numpy, rust, js, react, browser, hand-python, hand-js, hand-rust): the number of the 11 transcripts equal to `rce run` per runner, with the rce of the run commit (after) and, for the seven emitted-code runners, with the rce of main at 8ce91cea (before).

predictions.P1: after: 11 of 11 for every runner; before: fewer than 11 for python, js, rust and browser (the import prints, nothing is exported, private items, `process` at load)
predictions.P2: emitted program lines exceed hand lines by a factor of at least 2 per language summed over the eight programs, and every emitted file carries a runtime of more than 1,500 counted lines
predictions.P3: glue per language is under 250 counted lines, and per-program glue is 0 lines in Python and JS and at most 2 in Rust
predictions.P4: no prediction is registered for the ns figures; the critique's cost claim is judged to hold for a language when the boundary share of the emitted code exceeds 50% for at least 5 of the 8 programs

falsifiers: P1 fails if any runner after the change gives fewer than 11; P2 fails if a summed ratio is below 2; P3 fails if any glue total is 250 or more or the per-program glue exceeds the bound
known_before_registration: during development on this machine all ten runners gave 11 of 11 with the changed emitter; with main's rce, python gave 2 of 11, js 0 of 11 and rust did not compile (E0603), browser stopped with ReferenceError: process is not defined. No line count, glue count or ns figure was computed before registration.
machine: the shared development container of this session (x86_64 Linux; other agents' jobs run at the same time, so the ns figures carry that noise and are not a benchmark of record); results/machine.txt records CPU, kernel and tool versions
reporting: RESULTS.md: the run commit, every figure of results/summary.md, which predictions held, and where critique 9 holds and where it does not; results/ keeps check-after.txt, check-before.txt, loc.json, bench-python.json, bench-js.json, bench-rust.json, machine.txt
limits: eight small programs, none with tasks, actors, par or fn main; hosts are single-writer; the hand versions are checked on the eleven streams only (they do not trap on overflow and have no fuel); PyTorch is not covered (not installed; numpy scalars stand for array libraries) and TypeScript is not covered (the React host is JavaScript); the Scala target is not covered.
